items.title: JoyNews gets results: Mahama intervenes, four arrested as Abesua galamsey-damaged bridge undergoes repairs
items.description: Four people have been arrested and are in police custody following JoyNews ’ exclusive report on the destruction of the only access bridge linking several communities in the Abesua Electoral Area of the Atwima Mponua District in the Ashanti Region. The development follows the intervention of President John Mahama and the Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr. Frank Amoakohene, after the report highlighted how illegal mining activities had cut off residents from essential services, markets and farmlands. JoyNews can confirm that authorities have begun remedial works on the damaged road, with the water that had overflowed onto the stretch drained and the clogged bridge cleared. The affected section is also being gravelled with boulders to improve access, while four suspects have been arrested in connection with the illegal mining activities and are currently in police custody. President John Mahama has acknowledged the report, confirming that the situation had been brought to his attention and citing the JoyNews coverage as an example of how public concerns reach his administration. Speaking on his approach to public feedback, the President said he monitors social media platforms, including TikTok, to identify concerns raised by citizens and ensure they are brought to the attention of the appropriate ministers for action. He maintained that he does not dismiss criticism of his government, including from people who believe it is taking the country in the wrong direction, noting that public feedback helps identify challenges and improve governance. Ashanti Regional Minister Frank Amoakohene confirmed the ongoing intervention, saying the runoff had been drained from the road, the clogged bridge cleared, and work on the affected stretch commenced. Background Residents of Abesua No. 1, Abesua No. 2, Nyamebekyere, Abrokyire and adjoining communities had been left virtually isolated after illegal mining activities caused the collapse of the bridge over River Kukubu. The bridge served as the only access route connecting the communities to the main road at Seribuso and Mankranso. A JoyNews visit to the area on Sunday, October 25, revealed that the bridge had completely caved in after illegal miners allegedly excavated and degraded land along the riverbanks. The resulting overflow had submerged sections of the road, making it extremely difficult for vehicles and motorcycles to access the communities. Residents also disclosed that some miners returned to the site later that evening with heavy machinery and attempted to redirect the water by pushing sand into the river channel, without reconstructing the collapsed bridge. The situation severely affected education, with pupils who commute daily to Atwima Asamang Basic School reportedly abandoning classes, particularly during periods of rainfall, because they could not cross the river. Trading activities were also disrupted, as traders struggled to reach market centres to restock goods, while those who managed to make the journey faced exorbitant transportation fares. Farmers in the area separately raised concerns about the destruction of their farmlands and the growing difficulty of accessing their farms because of roads blocked by illegal mining operations. Some residents further alleged that they had faced intimidation and threats from illegal miners and their bodyguards whenever they attempted to challenge the activities. The farmers also accused some community leaders of complicity and raised concerns about alleged police involvement, calling for urgent investigations and stronger action to protect their livelihoods. They said previous attempts by residents to seize equipment used for illegal mining had failed, as the machinery often returned to the area shortly afterwards. Although the arrests and ongoing road repairs offer some relief, residents are expected to look to the authorities for sustained action to stop illegal mining, restore the damaged bridge and safeguard their farms and livelihoods.

items.title: NAIMOS intensifies operations against illegal mining in Western and Eastern Regions
items.description: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has intensified enforcement operations against illegal mining in the Western and Eastern Regions, targeting activities in forest reserves, farming areas and along critical water bodies. Separate operations on October 29, at Cape Three Points Forest in Ahanta West, Abrokyire-Krobo in Wassa Amenfi East, and the Apapam-Asikem area in Abuakwa South resulted in the arrest of 11 suspected illegal miners and the destruction of significant illegal mining infrastructure. At Cape Three Points Forest in the Ahanta West Municipality, NAIMOS personnel discovered illegal miners operating at several locations across the forest. At the first site, the Task Force destroyed four chanfang machines and seven water pumps, and arrested four suspected illegal miners, who were subsequently handed over to the police for further investigation. Further patrols led to another major site, where the operators had fled before the Task Force arrived. Two excavators were found at the site, but their monitors had already been removed. The Task Force destroyed three additional chanfang machines, four water pumps and four makeshift structures, and recovered a critical component from one of the excavators. In a separate operation at Abrokyire-Krobo in the Wassa Amenfi East Municipality, a NAIMOS Task Force raided an illegal mining site after the operators fled upon sighting personnel. The operation destroyed five chanfang machines, five water pumps, seven generator plants and two makeshift structures. An additional chanfang machine and water pump were recovered from the site. The patrol also observed renewed mining activity in some areas, underscoring the need for sustained monitoring and repeated enforcement to prevent miners from reoccupying previously disrupted locations. In the Eastern Region, NAIMOS conducted operations in the Apapam-Asikem area of the Abuakwa South Municipality, targeting illegal mining activities affecting the Birim River and its tributaries, as well as areas adjacent to the Atiwa Forest Reserve. The operation resulted in the arrest of seven suspected illegal miners and the destruction of two chanfang machines, three water pumps and three makeshift structures. NAIMOS assessments indicate that illegal miners continue to exploit remote, difficult terrain along water bodies to evade enforcement. NAIMOS says the operations demonstrate its commitment to expanding and maintaining pressure across water bodies, forest reserves, farms and other illegal mining hotspots, rather than concentrating enforcement on a single location. It says it will continue with intelligence-led, sustained operations to prevent the reoccupation of cleared sites, disrupt illegal mining logistics and protect critical environmental assets.

items.title: 48 terrorists, one soldier killed in foiled attacks on troops in Borno, Yobe
items.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Barely 24 hours when scores of Boko Haram/ISWAP terrorists were killed in separate encounter in communities of Kukawa and Marte local government areas of Borno state, about 48 terrorists were neutralised by Troops of the Joint Task Force, North East, Operation HADIN KAI while attempting to infiltrate military positions in Bitta Gwoza LGA of Borno State and North East Theatre Training School (NETTS), Buni Yadi, Gujba LGA of Yobe State between 29 and 30 October 2026. Unfortunately, the engagements recorded one soldier who paid the supreme sacrifice, with two others sustained minor injuries. This was disclosed on Friday in a press statement signed by the Acting Media Information Officer Headquarters Joint Task Force North East Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni. He said: “Troops of OPHK have dealt a major blow to Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorists, foiling their attacks on military positions in Bitta Gwoza LGA of Borno State and North East Theatre Training School (NETTS), Buni Yadi, Gujba LGA of Yobe State between 29 and 30 October 2026. “In Bitta, troops decisively disorganised an attempted terrorist assault on the night of 29 October 2026. The combined response of ground troops and air support overwhelmed the attackers, thwarting their plan and inflicting heavy casualties. “In a related development, troops launched a successful counter-attack against a large concentration of ISWAP fighters who attacked NETTS Buni Yadi on same 29 October to the early hours on 30 October 2026. “The approximately five-hour engagement was coordinated by the Theatre Command, with effective integration of Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition and Reconnaissance (ISTAR) capabilities, alongside air and ground assets. “The decisive counter-offensive resulted in 48 terrorists killed, with troops recovering a substantial cache of weapons and ammunition. “Recovered items include 42 AK-47 rifles, five PKT machine guns, four General Purpose Machine Guns (GPMG), one 60mm mortar, 105 AK-47 magazines and two video cameras. “Also recovered were 30 rounds of 12.7mm armour-piercing incendiary ammunition, 2,738 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, 223 rounds of 7.62mm NATO ammunition and 2,054 rounds of PKT ammunition. “The engagements recorded one soldier who paid the supreme sacrifice. May his soul rest in peace. Also the two others who sustained minor injuries are responding to treatment. The morale of troops remains high as they sustain operations against terrorist elements across the theatre”. Goni stated. The latest operational successes according to the statement further demonstrate the troops’ combat effectiveness, operational coordination and determination to deny terrorists freedom of action. The heavy losses suffered by the insurgents and the recovery of their weapons and ammunition Goni said, constitute another significant setback to their operational capabilities. items.title: Spanish transport minister refuses to resign over second major train crash on his watch
items.description: Spain’s transport minister on Friday rejected calls for his resignation over the second train accident on his watch to cause mass casualties this year, as authorities worked to identify the victims from a crash that left at least 69 dead. Lawmakers from across the political spectrum this week condemned Transport Minister Oscar Puente for attributing Wednesday’s crash to a break in protocol by control centre operators rather than accepting responsibility, with rail workers’ unions calling for his immediate dismissal. The crash, which happened near the town of Urda in central Spain, followed another accident involving the same rail companies on the same line that left 46 dead in January. It has reopened a debate about safety and maintenance on Spain’s high-speed rail network, the most extensive in Europe, as the country prepares for an election that left-leaning Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has called for November 29. “My duty now is not to focus on discussing whether I will remain in office, but on solving the problem, determining exactly what happened and providing clear explanations,” Puente said at a press conference on Friday. The train that smashed into a second stationary one was travelling at a speed between 160 and 200 kph when the collision occurred, according to a preliminary report released on Thursday by the Independent Authority for the Technical Investigation of Accidents and Incidents (AITAT). “The sequence of malfunctions, instructions, and actions eventually led to the collision, in the absence of the necessary mitigating barriers,” AITAT said in the report. AITAT said it would not be able to confirm the exact speed of the train until it extracted information from the train’s black box. At the scene of the crash, large cranes were lifting the mangled wreckage as the Civil Guard listed 64 people as missing in what is already Spain’s deadliest train accident since 2013 . Authorities have carried out 49 autopsies so far and formally identified five people — three women and two men — Esther Padilla, spokesperson for the Castilla-La Mancha regional government, said on state television network TVE . “Testing is proceeding slowly, although families will be contacted throughout the day so that they can come and collect their results,” Padilla said on Friday. It was unclear if all those missing were accounted for in the death toll. Authorities can’t rule out more fatalities No additional bodies were found when rescue teams overturned a train carriage on Thursday, Castilla-La Mancha regional leader Emiliano Garcia-Page said on TVE . Identifying the bodies was proving difficult because many were in pieces, he said. On Thursday, rescue teams had placed partial remains in 31 bags. “The truth is that we cannot rule out the possibility that there may be more fatalities,” Garcia-Page said. As identification of the dead continued, the debate about who was at fault intensified, with unions saying it was unfair to lay the blame on human error. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Friday vowed to find out what caused the accident. “It is unacceptable for a country like Spain, with such a strong high-speed rail system, to suffer two accidents of this nature and magnitude in a single year,” he said. The collision occurred after several trains were automatically stopped due to the failure of a signalling system, after which the central control centre in Madrid took over. A train operated by state-owned Renfe was authorised to proceed, even though there was a stationary Iryo-operated train ahead, according to Puente. Audio of communications between the control centre and the train drivers obtained by El Pais showed how a controller authorised the Renfe train to continue on its journey at a normal speed, which Puente said disregarded a protocol to travel at no more than 40 kph in such circumstances. The audio also showed the controller authorised the Renfe train, carrying 379 passengers and seven crew, to resume its journey even though the Iryo train, carrying 147 passengers and five crew, should have proceeded first according to protocol. Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente speaks during a press conference to provide details on the deadly train crash near Toledo, in Madrid, Spain, on October 30, 2026. — Reuters Controllers say focus should be on failed signal system Raquel Ayllón, a union leader for state-owned infrastructure operator Adif, said controllers were having to operate under difficult working conditions. “Human error is being criticised and questioned very quickly, while people are not really focusing on the central issue: the failure of the safety system,” Ayllón said on TVE . The LZB system which failed, triggering the sequence of events that led to Wednesday’s crash, was behind schedule for an upgrade, public documents show. In September 2021, Adif awarded a contract to Thales Espana, the Spanish arm of the French equipment maker, to complete the installation of a new, standardised European system called ERTMS by early 2026 for 93.8 million euros ($105m), according to press releases on the tender. The system has been installed across most of Spanish high-speed rail, according to a factsheet by European rail association UNIFE, which developed the new ERTMS standard. But the Madrid-Seville line, site of two fatal crashes, had fallen behind, according to the tender contract. The contract was passed to Hitachi Rail in 2024, according to Thales, which declined to provide comment on the delay of the rollout.

items.title: Arbitrage marocain : Abderrahim El Arjoune nommé directeur technique national
items.description: La Ligue nationale de football professionnel (LNFP) a annoncé la nomination d’Abderrahim El Arjoune au poste de directeur technique national de l’arbitrage, en remplacement de Redouane Jiyed. Ce dernier sera désormais chargé de la formation et de la formation continue des arbitres. Un changement à la tête de la direction technique de l’arbitrage marocain. La Ligue nationale de football professionnel (LNFP) a désigné Abderrahim El Arjoune comme nouveau directeur technique national de l’arbitrage, en remplacement de Redouane Jiyed, a annoncé la Fédération Royale Marocaine de Football (FRMF) dans un communiqué. Cette nomination s’inscrit dans le cadre des efforts visant à donner un nouvel élan à l’arbitrage national, à renforcer les mécanismes de développement de ce secteur et à améliorer le niveau des arbitres marocains. De son côté, Redouane Jiyed se voit confier une nouvelle mission axée sur la formation et la formation continue des arbitres. Ce choix tient compte de son expérience professionnelle et de l’expertise acquise au fil de son parcours dans l’arbitrage aux niveaux continental et international. À travers cette réorganisation, les instances du football national entendent renforcer l’encadrement technique et améliorer les dispositifs de formation, dans un contexte où la qualité de l’arbitrage demeure un enjeu majeur pour le développement du football marocain. items.title: 29-year-old Nigerian man killed as tree crushes car in London
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A 29-year-old Nigerian man, James Abiwon, has died after a tree fell on his car during Storm Boelo in Mill Hill, north London. According to Metro UK, Abiwon was driving along Dollis Road at about 12.30pm on Sunday when the tree came down in strong winds. Emergency crews, including police officers, firefighters, paramedics and an air ambulance, responded, but he was pronounced dead at the scene. His cousin, Tyrrell Okolo, described him as “a master of everything” and a devoted family man. Abiwon was a tech sales executive who had earned a degree from the University of Essex. He was also a semi-professional footballer with Aldershot, a musician with about 40,000 YouTube viewers and a mentor to many, his cousin said. Abiwon had been preparing to celebrate his 30th birthday with a padel tournament. The event will now go ahead in his memory, with proceeds going to support his family. His close friend, Kwame Affum, 29, said the two had played padel together just two days before the crash. “I’m trying hard to get my head around this,” he told Metro UK. A friend had messaged Abiwon shortly before the accident about money they owed him for the court, but he did not reply, prompting concern. Affum said Abiwon loved sport, was a good footballer and supported Arsenal. He had earned a first-class university degree and recently won an award at work. “He was full of energy and talent,” Affum said. “He was going to celebrate his 30th birthday in two weeks. It just seems impossible this has happened.” A witness who laid flowers at the scene told Metro UK that she heard a helicopter and went outside to find the fallen tree covering the road, with the car trapped beneath it. Abiwon’s girlfriend and best friend arrived while rescuers were still at the scene. The witness said they were shaking as they waited and hoped he would be brought out. The witness said Abiwon’s aunties and other relatives arrived later and were inconsolable. She described him as clearly well loved and said the community had lost one of its own. Traffic on Dollis Road was reportedly heavy at the time, as roadworks on a nearby street had diverted more vehicles onto the route. A neighbour whose home overlooks the scene said: “If it had been 10 minutes later, it could have been me.” The Metropolitan Police said officers were called to Dollis Road at about 12.40pm on Sunday after reports that a tree had fallen onto a moving car. Police are working with the local authority and coroner to establish the circumstances surrounding Abiwon’s death. Storm Boelo brought gusts of up to 84mph across parts of the UK over the weekend. A 60-year-old man was also killed by a falling tree in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland, while others were injured. Plus de 6,5 millions de F CFA en faux billets saisis
items.description: La Police judiciaire de Birni N’Konni du Niger, a interpellé, le vendredi 23 octobre 2026, un individu en possession de 6 520 000 F CFA en faux billets de banque, selon un communiqué de l'institution policière. Selon les premières investigations, cette importante somme devait être convertie en nairas avant d’être transférée au Nigeria. Un important coup de filet contre la fausse monnaie au Niger. La Police judiciaire de Birni N’Konni, dans la région de Tahoua, a mis la main sur 6 520 000 F CFA en faux billets, tous en coupures de 10 000 F CFA. L’opération a permis l’interpellation d’un individu au marché hebdomadaire de cette localité, le vendredi 23 octobre 2026. L’information a été rendue publique, ce vendredi 30 octobre 2026 par la Police. D’après les premières investigations, les faux billets étaient destinés à être convertis en nairas, la monnaie nigériane, avant leur transfert vers le Nigeria. Les déclarations du suspect interpellé feraient également état de l’implication présumée d’autres individus dans cette opération. Des éléments qui orientent les enquêteurs vers l’existence possible d’un réseau de fabrication ou de circulation de fausse monnaie. Dans sa communication, la Police nationale a salué la vigilance de l’Association des Agents de Change, dont la prompte réaction a contribué à l’interpellation du suspect. Elle a, par ailleurs, indiqué que les investigations se poursuivent afin de retrouver les autres personnes susceptibles d’être impliquées dans ce réseau présumé. À travers cette opération, la Police nationale réaffirme sa détermination à lutter contre toutes les formes de criminalité. Elle invite, dans le même élan, les populations à maintenir leur collaboration avec les Forces de défense et de sécurité pour contribuer à la préservation de la sécurité publique. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Plus de 6,5 millions de F CFA en faux billets saisis est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Self-Help Needs Help
items.description: In retrospect , 2016, the year that Angela Duckworth published Grit: The Power of Passion and Perseverance , may have been a high-water mark for the dogged go-getter‑ism she was selling. Her book landed just as Hillary Clinton, that avatar of tenacity, seemed poised to win the presidency and Alexander Hamilton was rapping on Broadway about not giving up his shot. You could still just barely discern within each of the billionaires who bestrode Silicon Valley the dork with unusual willpower who had made it. And among the books clustered near Grit in airport bookstores—where the American self is apparently at its most moldable—were other pitches for individual hardiness, including efforts to make Stoicism hot again. When I read Grit now, it feels to me like a taunt. Economic mobility has stalled, nonhumans are encroaching on our jobs, and COVID has scarred us with the knowledge that the unforeseen can creep up at any moment. You can be as gritty as sandpaper and still feel trampled on. Duckworth herself now seems ready to concede that our mind alone can’t control the direction of our life, that it doesn’t all happen “from the inside out,” as she put it in Grit . Back then, she arrived at the not-quite-mind-blowing conclusion that to be “the best of the best”—as accomplished as Olympic swimmers, Scripps National Spelling Bee champions, the president of Cinnabon—you had to really care about winning and work hard at it. “Today I wake up every day asking the same question that led me to psychology in the first place: Why are some people more successful than others? ” she writes in her new book, Situated: Find the People and Places That Bring Out Your Best . “But I no longer believe that a complete answer begins and ends with the individual.” Adam Grant, another best-selling psychologist, appears to have hit a similar wall. In Vibe: The Secrets of Strong Connections in a Lonely World , his sixth book, he departs from his relentless focus on self-transformation and looks instead at “the quality of connection between people.” For an author whose previous books are mostly about remaking yourself in the image of superachievers (he, too, has a thing for elite swimmers), this new endeavor feels like a departure: to consider that mercurial thing that happens between us and other people. Duckworth and Grant are colleagues at the University of Pennsylvania (he is at the Wharton School). They are also both associated with positive psychology, the field created by Martin Seligman at the school in the late 1990s—Seligman was Duckworth’s dissertation adviser. He rejected psychology’s focus on mental illness and wanted to identify the conditions under which human “flourishing” happens. Positive psychology was, at least in its own self-understanding, trying to apply empirical science to the ancient philosophical question of how to live a good life; Seligman wanted, as he recently wrote , to see if the field could “make the world a better place.” But the approach underwent something of a corporate transformation as it migrated into business schools and HR departments. One of Duckworth’s first grit studies examined the kind of cadet who thrives at West Point , and Grant looked at businesses such as Google and Facebook. Their evidence base, case studies, and examples continued to be drawn overwhelmingly from schools, companies, elite performers, and athletes (all those swimmers). What they were measuring was how you maximize performance, which is some distance from Aristotle. By the time the psychologists each strapped on a microphone and took to the TED stage in the 2010s with compressed, bullet-point versions of their research, they were ready for the self-help-book section. Their arrival helped give a glow-up to an enterprise that has thrived from the start on the notion that your inner resources alone, properly unearthed and deployed, will propel you to become the most successful version of you. In Self-Help (1859), the book that gave the genre its name, the Scottish journalist Samuel Smiles wrote that “help from without is often enfeebling in its effects, but help from within invariably invigorates.” What method did advice-givers deploy? Extract formulas for inner drive from vivid models of extraordinary achievement, and never mind how much gets left out—those pesky forces of genetics and upbringing, economics and history, not to mention luck. Duckworth and Grant joined in, and their best sellers got blurbed by the business and media elite (Mark Cuban, Oprah Winfrey, Sheryl Sandberg, Arianna Huffington). Yet now they seem to be swerving onto more unruly terrain. Are their new books, I wondered, prepared to question some of the tenets of the venerable self-made-man myth? A person’s social world, the one outside their control that impinges on them at every turn, would seem to be key to understanding a rise or fall. Is that what Situated and Vibe , products of a disorienting moment, would do: look around and realize how little power we actually have over the course of our own lives? That isn’t what these books do. Grant does acknowledge the “uncertainty, complexity, and conflict” that characterize most of our encounters once we leave the confines of our mind. “Like it or not,” Duckworth now pauses to observe, “our every thought and action is profoundly shaped by our peers and mentors, by our culture, and even by the objects in our personal space.” Entire centuries-old fields of social science, as the authors both know well, have detailed how such forces influence us. But recognizing constraint and limitation is not what this genre is about. Its goal is to reassure us that we have ultimate control over our fate. Grant’s focus is on vibing, a word he uses to describe that ephemeral state when people or a group connect deeply—when “conversations pulse with energy. Thoughts soar. Trust grows. Time flies.” He insists that this is a “skill set that can be learned and taught,” and that it is crucial to one’s success. What follows is an assortment of studies to establish the ideal conditions for generating this crucial synergistic energy. In one of them , the same woman approached two different groups of male hikers trekking through a rainforest and, after asking them to fill out a questionnaire, she tore off a piece of paper, wrote down her number, and handed it to each of them. She met the first group on an ordinary bridge, and only one in eight men later called. But half of the men in the second group, which she encountered on a narrow suspension bridge swaying 230 feet above churning rapids, called her. The takeaway? What deepens a relationship is being in an “emotionally intense situation.” Again and again, Grant plucks broad lessons from social-psychology experiments so odd that I came away wondering how big the sample size could possibly be, whether correlation and causation were getting confused—and, not least, how to apply the findings. Grant proposes engineering a group outing to such a bridge or a haunted house or, God help me, an improv-comedy class. Unlike his earlier books, which are largely about shifting one’s mindset, there is only so much you can do to master your environment or other people, though Grant makes lots of suggestions. Throw dinner parties, but ensure that they are “carefully choreographed.” For example, ask guests to each throw one shoe in a pile and then take turns grabbing a shoe and holding it up for the owner to claim. “At dessert time, I prompted people to play musical chairs,” he proudly reports. I guess trust grew during these pre-K games? Often Grant slips into a style that reads like a manual for robots learning how to act like humans. “Laughing during and after disagreements,” he advises, “is one of the most effective ways to maintain a healthy bond.” But you can’t really reverse engineer something like vulnerability or attentiveness or love. Grant’s attempt to script and quantify the ineffable connections among “associates, allies, pals, and companions”—his byzantine taxonomy of vibers—just seems condescending. Isn’t it the truest of truisms to say that “relying on our first impressions is shortsighted”? His tendency to end sections on a sententious note only adds to the patronizing tone. “A strong bond can last for years,” he intones, “but forming one doesn’t have to take years. Sometimes a little heat is enough to build a blazing fire.” Duckworth’s approach is more schematic, conveyed succinctly by a “Three Boxes Model”: “Situation,” “Thoughts,” and “Response.” To take her most basic example, if you put your workout clothes where you can see them (situation), exercise will come to mind (thoughts), and because “changing your thoughts, in turn, automatically changes your behavior,” you’ll go for a jog (response). At a small scale, sure, this works: If you want to eat better, place carrots and apples around the house. But Duckworth goes bigger. In Grit , she made the case for personal agency; here, she’s introducing “situational agency.” “Like the best of the best, you, too, can proactively seek out situations optimized to achieve your fullest potential,” she writes. If you don’t like the culture in which you’re embedded, if it’s cramping that potential, go elsewhere. Rearrange your environment for maximum grittiness. Yet her guidance is strangely out of touch. Among her case studies, she focuses on, who else, an Olympic swimmer, Léon Marchand, and his decision to move from France to Tempe, Arizona, so that he could train with a world-renowned coach. Keep in mind that both of Marchand’s parents, as well as an uncle, were Olympic swimmers; that he had joined a swim club at age 6; and that he had already placed sixth in the 2020 Summer Olympics in Tokyo before his move. From this fine-tuned trajectory—he went on to win four gold medals—Duckworth concludes that anything is possible for any of us if we just change our location: “In those moments when your challenge seems daunting, ask yourself, what would Léon do? And remember what he did do: Léon Marchand got on a plane.” Never mind that relocating is hardly simple for anyone. Is our own situation always so clear to us? And if you change it, how do you know you’re making it better and not worse? Duckworth advises parents who want to improve their children’s opportunities to consider moving to school districts with better teachers and more resources, even if it means living in a smaller home. What if the child gets bullied at that new school? What if they resent having to share a room with their annoying sibling? Every circumstance in a person’s life is multidimensional. Describing the many factors at work is daunting enough, but pinpointing what can (and should) be changed is like trying to yank a tablecloth from a set table without breaking any dishes. Duckworth doesn’t see the problem. She has yet more boxes, these for items labeled “uncontrollable” and “controllable,” as if the two can always and easily be parsed. The effects of “the modern world” and “your genes” (uncontrollable) get put in one category, and “the culture of where you work and live now” and “your mindset” (controllable) get put in another. I did a double take when I saw these neat divisions. Had Duckworth just cracked the great mystery of nature versus nurture? One of the more nonsensical studies she cites found that growing up in a household with 500 books had the equivalent effect on a child’s “lifetime educational attainment” as having college-educated parents. How did this study even work? Can you isolate the effects of the books? Who else but college-educated parents would fill their house with that many books? Duckworth is not concerned with such details. The lesson lies in having books around (controllable), and she lectures parents accordingly: “Situationally wise parents don’t rush out to buy their children the latest iPhone. Instead, they purchase as many books as they can afford, line their walls with bookshelves and not TV screens, and take their children to the library on weekends.” Duckworth and Grant have fallen into the same self-help trap. Situated and Vibe gesture at the realm beyond our immediate power, but they are still about how we can flex our willpower for the sake of more and more success. Duckworth refers approvingly to the Serenity Prayer, but she seems to miss what actually makes it meaningful. This is a prayer for people working on accepting their smallness and fallibility—it was popularized by recovering alcoholics. It is a prayer of realism, not ambition. The possibility of change exists, but only once you recognize and embrace the notion that many things will always be impossible to change. Every self-help book is also an autobiography, even if unintentionally so. Why should we listen to such writers if they haven’t faced and overcome the problems they purport to solve? Both Duckworth and Grant reveal themselves as obsessive overachievers. Both went to Harvard. Duckworth was a consultant at McKinsey, then had stints teaching middle and high school before getting her Ph.D. in psychology. Grant’s friends called him Mr. Facts as a kid—he was the boy who fired off baseball statistics when they were just trying to trade cards. Despite his fear of heights, in high school he became a springboard diver good enough to be in the Junior Olympics. He got his master’s and doctorate in three years . There’s nothing wrong with being driven. But compulsively performance-oriented people—in my experience, at least—find it hard to resist monitoring their behavior until there are zero unknowns. Grant hinted at this internal struggle in a 2013 New York Times Magazine profile : “For me, in my moments of idleness, I experience the most existential anxiety, so I like that every moment is scheduled, even when it’s having on my calendar that I’m going to watch a television show with my wife. It means my brain is engaged in other things, and it’s not going to be a terrifying evening.” This frantic need to conquer uncertainty comes through in his books. He starts with humility, but what follows is an intense self-surveillance, a search for objective measures of how he’s doing. As he began writing for a popular audience, he has recalled, he pined for his diver days, when he was meticulously rated on the size of the splash as he entered the water. So he assembled colleagues to rate every new article and book chapter he produced on a scale of zero to 10. Look around at all that resists being easily tweaked toward “excellence”—not least other people and reality itself—and the limits of self-help appear unavoidable. Duckworth reveals this at one point in Situated , in a way that I’m not sure she even realizes. In a genuinely vulnerable moment, she recounts a marital crisis after a lifetime of assuming that, with enough grit, she could manage everything. When her husband’s real-estate-development company encountered hard times, their relationship frayed; she cried herself to sleep every night and contemplated separation. Following the advice of her book, Duckworth reports that much of the solution lay in shifting the elements in box one, altering their schedules and restructuring their work life to create a new situation: Now they could “sleep, exercise, and laugh a little every single day .” But that doesn’t seem to be what really saved them. She also describes all the therapy they undertook, with “tremendous reluctance” on her part—and with three therapists: one for her, one for her husband, and another for both of them. This is not changing the situation. Therapy is about better understanding yourself within a situation, tracing your patterns, learning to see others better as well. The work entailed is not optimization. It’s about dropping illusions. For Duckworth and her husband, it meant articulating the “messy bits,” the “sadness, confusion, fear, and doubt that each of us had been carrying in silence.” Doing what Léon Marchand would do—get on a plane to another city—was precisely not the point. Every time I toggled between reading these books and opening the newspaper, I was reminded of just how inadequate their self-help message feels for this moment. When Duckworth and Grant talk about “culture”—which they do, a lot—they’re often referring to the highly controllable, measurable, top-down cultures of sports teams, tech companies, consulting firms. Their books’ neatness does not leave room for the feeling of being completely stuck, individually and collectively, and also buffeted by a world swirling out of our control. Most days, I feel like Alex in A Clockwork Orange , strapped into a chair, eyelids held open, forced to watch norms collapse, economies rupture, ecosystems crumble. Personal or situational agency sounds great, but maybe what we really need is moral agency. Grant has occasionally garnished his stories of start-up successes with mentions of such leaders as Martin Luther King Jr. and Nelson Mandela, to curiously dispiriting effect: The struggle to reshape values and society blurs into having a good pitch deck and some move-fast-and-break-things gumption. It’s the abiding ethos of expediency and mastery that limits the self-helpfulness of these new books—their emphasis on getting somewhere quickly and knowing with total certainty that you have arrived. Is that the point of fulfilling work, of satisfying family life, of friendship, of really anything worth doing? This article appears in the December 2026 print edition with the headline “Self-Help Needs Help.”

items.title: Interview : « Il faut agir rapidement dès les premiers signes d’AVC » (Pr Mofou Belo)
items.description: L’accident vasculaire cérébral (AVC) est une urgence médicale qui peut toucher toute personne, quel que soit son âge. Au Togo, cette maladie représente une préoccupation importante de santé publique. Selon l’Annuaire des statistiques sanitaires 2023 du ministère en charge de la Santé, les formations sanitaires du pays ont enregistré 4 756 consultations et 1 924 hospitalisations liées aux AVC, ainsi que 365 décès dus à cette maladie. Face à cette maladie, Pr Mofou Belo, chef division de la surveillance des maladies non transmissibles au ministère en charge de la Santé, explique les signes à reconnaître, les gestes à adopter et les moyens de prévention. ATOP : Qu’est-ce qu’un accident vasculaire cérébral ? Pr Mofou Belo Pr Mofou Belo : L’AVC survient lorsqu’un vaisseau sanguin qui alimente le cerveau se bouche par un caillot ou se rompt. Dans les deux cas, une partie du cerveau ne reçoit plus normalement le sang et l’oxygène et le glucose dont elle a besoin pour fonctionner. On distingue principalement l’AVC ischémique, causé par l’obstruction d’une artère par un caillot, et l’AVC hémorragique, provoqué par sa rupture. C’est une urgence médicale, car les lésions peuvent s’aggraver rapidement si la personne n’est pas prise en charge dans un délai de moins de 4 heures car chaque minute compte. Quels sont les principaux facteurs qui favorisent cette maladie ? L’hypertension artérielle est l’un des principaux facteurs de risque. Le diabète, l’excès de cholestérol, l’obésité, le manque d’activité physique et certaines maladies du cœur peuvent également favoriser la survenue d’un AVC. Le tabac et la consommation excessive d’alcool augmentent aussi ces risques. La grande majorité de ces facteurs de risque sont évitables. Il est donc important de surveiller régulièrement sa santé et de suivre les traitements prescrits lorsqu’on souffre d’une maladie chronique en se rendant chez un médecin. Quelle est l’ampleur du problème au Togo ? Les données disponibles montrent que les AVC constituent un véritable problème de santé dans notre pays. Une étude réalisée dans des centres hospitaliers togolais et publiée en 2023 estime l’incidence à 79,6 cas pour 100 000 habitants par an. Elle rapporte également une mortalité de 27,5 % parmi les patients étudiés. Ces chiffres doivent être interprétés dans leur contexte : ils proviennent de données hospitalières et ne représentent pas nécessairement l’ensemble des cas survenus dans le pays. Comment reconnaître les premiers signes d’un AVC ? Les signes apparaissent souvent brutalement. La personne peut ressentir une faiblesse ou une paralysie du bras, de la jambe ou d’un côté du corps. Son visage peut se déformer, sa parole peut devenir difficile ou incompréhensible. Elle peut aussi perdre soudainement la vue, avoir des difficultés à garder l’équilibre ou présenter des troubles de la compréhension. Certaines personnes peuvent avoir des vertiges ou des maux de tête violents. Devant l’un de ces signes, il ne faut pas attendre de voir si la situation va s’améliorer. Même si les symptômes disparaissent après quelques minutes, une consultation médicale urgente reste nécessaire. Que faut-il faire lorsqu’on soupçonne un AVC chez un proche ? Il faut conduire la personne sans délai vers une structure de santé capable de la prendre en charge. Il ne faut surtout pas attendre le lendemain, ni perdre du temps avec des remèdes traditionnels ou une automédication. Chaque minute compte, car plus la prise en charge est rapide, plus les chances de limiter les lésions cérébrales sont importantes. Il est également utile de noter l’heure à laquelle les premiers signes sont apparus et de communiquer cette information aux soignants. Il ne faut surtout pas tenter de donner des médicaments conseillés par une tiers personne. Lorsque l’AVC survient en pleine nuit il ne faut pas attendre le lever du sommeil avant de se diriger vers une structure de santé. L’AVC concerne-t-il uniquement les personnes âgées ? Non. Même si le risque augmente avec l’âge, les personnes jeunes voir des enfants peuvent également être touchées. Certaines maladies, notamment celles qui affectent le cœur ou le sang, peuvent favoriser la survenue d’un AVC chez des personnes plus jeunes. Il ne faut donc pas considérer que cette maladie ne concerne que les personnes âgées. Quel que soit l’âge, l’apparition soudaine de signes évocateurs doit conduire à consulter en urgence. Ce n’est pas la peine de perdre le temps dans les centres de prière. Allez directement à l’hôpital, d’autres personnes peuvent prier pour vous, en votre absence, pendant que vous prendrez la direction d’une structure de santé proche de votre domicile ; chaque minute compte ! Quelles peuvent être les conséquences d’un AVC sur la vie du malade ? Les conséquences varient selon la partie du cerveau touchée et la gravité de l’AVC. Certaines personnes gardent une paralysie toute leur vie, ont des difficultés à parler, à se déplacer ou à accomplir seules les gestes du quotidien. D’autres peuvent présenter des troubles de la mémoire ou de la concentration. La récupération dépend notamment de la rapidité de la prise en charge et de la rééducation. L’accompagnement doit être adapté à chaque patient et peut faire intervenir plusieurs professionnels de santé, avec le soutien de la famille, ou des proches. Comment réduire les risques d’AVC au quotidien ? La prévention commence par le contrôle des facteurs de risque. Il faut faire vérifier régulièrement sa tension artérielle, surveiller sa glycémie (taux de sucre dans le sang) et son taux de cholestérol lorsque cela est nécessaire, et prendre correctement les médicaments prescrits. Une alimentation équilibrée, moins riche en sel et en graisses, la consommation de cinq fruits et légumes ainsi qu’une activité physique régulière, 30 mn, 3 fois par semaine, contribuent aussi à protéger la santé. Il est conseillé d’éviter le tabac et de limiter l’alcool. Les personnes qui souffrent d’hypertension ou de diabète doivent poursuivre leur suivi médical, même lorsqu’elles se sentent bien ou en forme. Chaque vie compte ! Quel message souhaitez-vous adresser à la population ? quels sont vos conseils. « AVC : chaque minute compte, chaque geste préventif compte, chaque vie compte ! » Prévenons l’AVC, reconnaissons ses signes, agissons vite. Le Togo reste uni contre les AVC ! Mon message se résume en trois points clés : d’abord prévenir l’AVC. Il s’agit de connaître sa tension artérielle, réduire le sel, bouger régulièrement et bien suivre ses traitements. Ensuite reconnaître l’AVC . Il est également important de savoir reconnaître les signes d’alerte qui imposent une réaction immédiate, tels qu’un visage déformé, bras faible, parole troublée. Enfin agir sans perdre de temps. Devant une suspicion d’AVC, rechercher immédiatement une prise en charge médicale adaptée, se rendre à l’hôpital par tous les moyens, ne pas attendre une amélioration spontanée. Mon conseil stratégique, en tant que coordonnateur du programme national de lutte contre les maladies non transmissibles, est que la lutte contre les AVC ne commence pas à l’hôpital, mais au sein des familles, au sein des communautés, par la prévention, le dépistage de l’hypertension artérielle et la connaissance des signes d’alerte. C’est cette responsabilisation de chaque citoyen qui peut contribuer durablement à réduire le fardeau des AVC au Togo. Chaque vie compte ; une vie perdue bêtement est une perte pour le pays, chaque citoyen compte pour la vie économique du pays. Il y a forcément un lien entre la santé et le développement économique. Propos recueillis par Abel OZIH

items.title: Torgbiga Addo IX sworn in as Paramount Chief of Klikor Traditional Area
items.description: The chiefs, elders and people of the Klikor Traditional Area have formally installed and sworn in Torgbiga Addo IX, Dr Frank Hukporti, as their Paramount Chief. He succeeds the late Torgbiga Addo VIII, who led the traditional area from 1983 until his death on January 14, 2026, at the age of 93. The late chief, who also served as President of the Klikor Traditional Council, was laid to rest on Saturday, October 24, 2026, following traditional funeral rites held during the preceding week. The formal installation and swearing-in of his successor took place on Sunday, October 25. Building on his predecessor’s legacy In a media engagement ahead of the ceremonies, Torgbiga Addo IX reflected on the legacy of his predecessor, highlighting his contributions to education and community development during his 43-year reign. An educationist who taught at a training college before ascending the stool, Torgbiga Addo VIII made education a central part of his leadership. Under his reign, basic schools were established in virtually every community within the traditional area. He also championed the establishment of Klikor Secondary Technical School (Klistec), where he served as the first headmaster. Through partnerships with non-governmental organisations and private institutions, he also facilitated the provision of potable water to communities across the area. Torgbiga Addo IX, a German-trained educationist and distinguished musicologist, has pledged to build on these achievements, with tertiary education among his priorities. He has expressed an ambition to establish a university in Klikor, citing the absence of a university in the Ketu South Municipality. He has also identified the improvement of road networks linking Klikor to neighbouring communities, including Agbozume and Aflao, as an urgent development priority. Profile of the new Paramount Chief Torgbiga Addo IX is a retired Deputy Commissioner of Police and former Director of Bands of the Ghana Police Service. He holds a PhD in Ethnomusicology from the University of Bayreuth in Germany and is credited with pioneering the concept of “Musical Domestication”. He is also the founder and coordinator of the Brass Band Festival at Klikor-Agbozume and has established himself as an educator, conductor and author. He maintains institutional links with the German Embassy and the Goethe-Institut in Accra. Vision for Klikor Klikor is one of the oldest Ewe settlements and is historically regarded as a spiritual centre, with several traditional shrines of significance. Its population is predominantly made up of peasant farmers and kente weavers. The new Paramount Chief has outlined a long-term vision of transforming Klikor into a modern city while pursuing UNESCO recognition for its historic shrines as a cultural heritage site. Several traditional rulers participated in or were acknowledged during the preparations and ceremonies. They included Togbiga Afede XIV of Asogli State in Ho, Torgbiga Tenge Dzokoto VII of Anyako, Togbiga Amenya Fiti V of Aflao, Torgbiga Adamah III of Agbozume, Torgbiga Akpo Ashiakpor VI of Weta and Torgbiga Wenya III of Anlo State. The announcement was issued by the chiefs, elders and people of the Klikor Traditional Area in the Ketu South Municipality of the Volta Region.

items.title: Ouverture au palais des congrès de la première édition du forum de la diaspora mauritanienne à l’étranger
items.description: La première édition du Forum des communautés mauritaniennes de l'étranger, s’est ouverte ce vendredi au palais des congrès « Mokhtar Ould Daddah » sous l'égide du président Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani et en présence de quelque 700 participants venus des quatre coins du monde. Organisé par le ministère des Affaires étrangères, de la Coopération africaine et des Mauritaniens de l’étranger, ce forum aborde des questions relatives à la situation des communautés et à leur rôle dans le soutien au développement national, ainsi qu’au renforcement de leur participation politique et économique. Le programme prévoit des ateliers consacrés aux droits des communautés et à leur participation politique, ainsi qu’aux moyens de développer leur représentation et de renforcer la communication avec elles, avec la participation de secteurs gouvernementaux et d’institutions nationales, parmi lesquelles les ministères des Affaires étrangères et de l’Intérieur, l’Assemblée nationale et la Commission nationale indépendante des élections. Un autre atelier se penchera sur le rôle des communautés dans la promotion du tourisme mauritanien, l’attraction d’investissements touristiques et la dynamisation des échanges commerciaux, avec la participation d’instances gouvernementales, d’institutions économiques et touristiques, ainsi que de représentants des missions diplomatiques et d’investisseurs. Le forum vise à renforcer les liens des Mauritaniens résidant à l’étranger avec leur pays d’origine, et à tirer parti de leurs expériences, de leurs compétences et de leurs réseaux internationaux pour soutenir le développement et faire connaître les atouts touristiques et d’investissement du pays.

items.title: FBI offers over N6m reward for information on wanted Nigerian woman
items.description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has announced a $5,000 (approximately ₦6.7 million per exchange rate as of when this report was published) reward for information leading to the arrest of a Nigerian woman, Emuobosan Emanuella Hall, who is wanted in the United States for failing to report to prison to serve a 96-month sentence over money laundering and fraud offences. Hall, who was born in Nigeria on October 10, 1980, was convicted of conspiracy to commit money laundering and conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud in connection with a romance scam involving multiple victims. According to the FBI, Hall was charged in April 2024 over her alleged role in laundering funds obtained from victims through the romance scam. She was arrested in Georgia and subsequently released on bond before pleading guilty to the charges. Hall was sentenced in January 2026 to 96 months (eight years) in federal prison. However, she failed to report to the designated correctional facility in March 2026 to begin serving her sentence, prompting US authorities to issue an arrest warrant. The FBI said a federal arrest warrant was issued on March 31, 2026, by the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana in New Orleans, following the bond violation charge. She was subsequently charged through a criminal complaint on April 14, 2026, with failure to appear for service of a sentence and was indicted on the same charge on October 23, 2026. The FBI said Hall also goes by the aliases Emuobosan E. Hall, Emuobosan Emanuella Erih and “Mobo”. The agency disclosed that she has links to Warri and Oleh in Delta State, as well as Abuja, Nigeria. She also has reported ties to London, Gloucester and Croydon in England, and Atlanta, Georgia, in the United States. According to her FBI wanted notice, Hall is 5 feet 6 inches tall, weighs approximately 87 kilogrammes, has black hair and brown eyes, and speaks English and some Yoruba. The FBI is offering a reward of up to $5,000, equivalent to approximately ₦6.73 million, for information leading to her arrest, based on an exchange rate of about ₦1,346.22 to the dollar on October 30, 2026. CxRates+1 The agency has urged anyone with information about Hall’s whereabouts to contact its nearest FBI office or the American Embassy or Consulate. items.title: Savanes : La 4e édition du Forum CJES en régions prend fin à Dapaong
items.description: Dapaong, 30 oct. (ATOP) – La 4 è édition du Forum de la Confédération des jeunes entreprises et startups du Togo (CJES Togo) en région a pris fin le vendredi 30 octobre à Dapaong, après trois jours d’activités consacrées à la promotion de l’entrepreneuriat, à l’insertion professionnelle des jeunes et à la transformation numérique des entreprises locales. Après les régions Maritime, des Plateaux et Centrale, le forum a achevé son parcours dans les Savanes. La rencontre est organisée en partenariat avec le ministère délégué chargé du Commerce et du Contrôle de la qualité. Elle est placée sous le thème : « Rassembler les entreprises en région pour transformer et protéger l’économie locale à l’ère du digital ». L’initiative vise à rapprocher les dispositifs d’accompagnement des entrepreneurs des différentes régions et à faciliter le développement des initiatives économiques des jeunes. L’évènement a été marqué par une mini foire d’exposition des produits locaux, des communications sur les avantages de la formalisation des petites et moyennes entreprises (PME) et des coopératives, les obligations fiscales et sociales ainsi que les mécanismes de collaboration entre les secteurs public et privé. Des ateliers pratiques ont permis aux participants de découvrir comment utiliser Facebook, Instagram et WhatsApp Business pour faire connaître leurs produits et développer leurs activités. Des porteurs de projets ont également présenté leurs initiatives. Certains ont bénéficié de chèques-services dont les montants varient de 100 000 à 1 500 000 F CFA. La dernière journée a été consacrée à la présentation des plateformes e-CJES et CJES Hub, destinées à accompagner les entrepreneurs. Elle a également donné lieu à un Job Dating régional organisé avec Talent2Africa et la Fondation Mastercard. L’objectif est de faciliter l’accès des jeunes diplômés à des expériences professionnelles rémunérées de 12 mois dans des entreprises locales. Visite des stands d’exposition Le gouverneur de la région des Savanes, Atcha-Dédji Affoh, a encouragé les jeunes entrepreneurs à profiter des opportunités offertes pour développer leurs activités. Le point focal de la CJES dans les Savanes, Dr Alassani Mohamed Cissé, a rappelé que les jeunes constituent une force importante pour la transformation de l’économie locale, à condition de bénéficier d’un accompagnement adapté, d’un accès aux opportunités et d’un cadre favorable à l’entrepreneuriat. La représentante de la représentante résidente du Fonds des Nations unies pour la population (UNFPA) au Togo, Mme Ameyo Letou, a insisté sur l’importance d’investir dans les compétences et le potentiel des jeunes, particulièrement des jeunes femmes. Elle a rappelé que leur insertion professionnelle doit aussi tenir compte de leur santé, de leurs droits et de leur épanouissement. Le forum a mobilisé les autorités administratives et locales, des partenaires techniques et financiers, des responsables d’entreprises, des startups, des coopératives ainsi que des jeunes diplômés en quête d’opportunités professionnelles. ATOP/JK/AO

items.title: Boffa: Yick Fung Shipping au chevet des pêcheurs artisanaux, un geste fort pour la sécurité maritime, la cohésion sociale
items.description: Du 20 au 23 octobre 2026, l’entreprise de transport maritime Yick Fung Shipping a organisé, dans la préfecture de Boffa, une cérémonie officielle de remise de dons en soutien aux pêcheurs artisanaux de 31 ports de pêche et sites de débarquement situés le long du fleuve Fatala. Cette initiative s’est accompagnée d’activités de sensibilisation aux règles de navigation et de formation à la sécurité maritime et à la prévention des accidents en mer. D’une durée totale de quatre jours, elle visait à renforcer les connaissances des pêcheurs en matière de sécurité maritime ainsi que leur capacité à réagir en cas d’urgence. La cérémonie de remise des dons s’est déroulée dans une atmosphère solennelle et conviviale, en présence du préfet de Boffa, du maire de Boffa, du directeur des affaires maritimes de Boffa, du directeur des pêches de Boffa, du commandant de la gendarmerie maritime de Boffa, du directeur de l’artisanat, du tourisme et de la culture de Boffa, du chef du bureau du littoral de Boffa et du chef du port central de pêche de Boffa. De nombreux jeunes, femmes et pêcheurs, bénéficiaires directs de cette action, y ont également pris part. Les dons comprenaient : （1）des équipements complets de protection individuelle destinés aux pêcheurs qui prennent la mer, notamment des gilets de sauvetage et des flotteurs (bouées de sauvetage) ; （2）plusieurs tonnes de riz et de sucre, ainsi que d’importantes quantités d’huile alimentaire, afin de contribuer à la sécurité alimentaire des familles de pêcheurs. Au-delà de l’aide matérielle, Yick Fung Shipping a accordé une attention particulière au renforcement des capacités des pêcheurs. Plusieurs séances de formation pratique dans le domaine maritime ont porté sur les thèmes suivants : （1） les bonnes pratiques pour naviguer en toute sécurité ; （2） les gestes élémentaires de premiers secours ; （3） l’utilisation correcte des équipements de protection ; （4） les mesures essentielles pour prévenir et éviter les accidents en mer. Prenant la parole, le maire de la commune urbaine de Boffa, Stell Soumah, a salué cette initiative et exprimé sa reconnaissance à la société Yick Fung Shipping pour son geste en faveur des communautés de pêcheurs. Il a encouragé le renforcement de ce type de partenariat, tout en plaidant pour un accompagnement durable des acteurs de la pêche artisanale, notamment dans les domaines de la sécurité, de l’accès aux équipements et de l’amélioration des conditions de travail. Pour l’autorité communale, la protection des pêcheurs exige une mobilisation collective, car la sécurité maritime ne peut être l’affaire d’un seul acteur. Prenant ensuite la parole, le directeur des affaires maritimes de Boffa, Joachim Faya Tounguino, a salué le sens des responsabilités de Yick Fung Shipping. Il a souligné que cette action s’inscrivait pleinement dans les orientations nationales visant à assurer la sécurité de la pêche artisanale et à réduire les risques en mer, en particulier pendant les périodes de forte activité de pêche. L’un des temps forts de la cérémonie a été l’intervention de Xu Yongshang, directeur du département de la culture d’entreprise du groupe COSCO SHIPPING. Son discours a illustré l’engagement de l’entreprise en matière de responsabilité sociale. Il a réaffirmé l’engagement de celle-ci à accompagner durablement le développement des communautés riveraines, à promouvoir la sécurité maritime et à soutenir le progrès socioéconomique local, dans un esprit de coopération, de respect mutuel et de bénéfices partagés : « En 2019, Yick Fung Shipping, filiale du groupe COSCO SHIPPING, s’est implantée en Guinée, où elle a pris racine. L’entreprise garde toujours à l’esprit sa responsabilité sociale et sait qu’elle ne saurait se développer sans le soutien des populations locales. Depuis sept ans, les employés de Yick Fung ont participé à plusieurs opérations de sauvetage en mer. L’entreprise a fait don d’engins de pêche, de bateaux de pêche et de produits de première nécessité aux pêcheurs et aux habitants, fourni des manuels scolaires et des articles d’hygiène aux écoles, et œuvré activement à la création d’emplois. Elle remercie tout particulièrement les services de l’administration placés sous l’autorité du préfet de Boffa, les sages, les habitants des communautés et nos amis pêcheurs pour leur amitié et leur soutien. Les activités professionnelles et les déplacements sur l’eau comportent des risques. Si les vents et les vagues sont impitoyables, la solidarité humaine, elle, demeure. Préserver la vie de chaque pêcheur et de chaque personne travaillant sur l’eau est une préoccupation que nous partageons tous. C’est pourquoi nous vous apportons des produits de première nécessité et du matériel de sécurité nautique, à savoir 289 sacs de riz, 289 sacs de sucre, 289 bidons d’huile alimentaire, 428 gilets de sauvetage et 221 flotteurs (bouées de sauvetage). Bien que leur valeur matérielle soit modeste, ces dons témoignent de notre attention sincère envers nos amis guinéens. Par cette modeste contribution, nous souhaitons renforcer la sécurité de nos frères et sœurs qui affrontent régulièrement les vents et les vagues, afin que chaque sortie en mer se termine par un retour sain et sauf. Nous souhaitons également apporter aux familles des communautés de quoi se nourrir et un peu de réconfort, pour qu’au-delà de leur dur labeur quotidien, elles ressentent la chaleur des liens de voisinage et le soutien qui les unit. » En retour, les pêcheurs bénéficiaires ont également exprimé leur gratitude envers la société donatrice et salué cette initiative. Ils se sont engagés à mettre en pratique, lors de leurs sorties quotidiennes en mer, les connaissances acquises pendant ces formations, à respecter rigoureusement les règles de sécurité et à protéger ainsi leur vie. Le chef du port central de Boffa, Idrissa Wattara Bangoura, a souligné l’importance de cet appui pour des professionnels quotidiennement exposés aux risques de la navigation, tout en réaffirmant la nécessité de poursuivre les actions de sensibilisation afin que chaque pêcheur puisse exercer son activité dans des conditions plus sûres. Interrogé à cette occasion, le préfet de Boffa, le colonel Mamadou Ciré Bah, a exprimé sa satisfaction et adressé ses remerciements à la société Yick Fung Shipping pour cet appui destiné aux communautés de pêcheurs. L’autorité préfectorale a rappelé que la sécurité maritime exige l’implication de tous : entreprises, autorités, responsables communautaires et professionnels de la mer. Elle a également encouragé les initiatives de solidarité susceptibles de contribuer à la protection des populations et au renforcement de la cohabitation pacifique entre les différents acteurs. Un appel à faire de la prévention, du dialogue et de la responsabilité partagée les piliers d’un développement local harmonieux. À travers cette initiative, Yick Fung Shipping a une nouvelle fois démontré son sens des responsabilités en tant qu’entreprise de transport maritime, en conjuguant développement économique, responsabilité sociale et soutien concret aux communautés de pêcheurs de Boffa.

items.title: Les villes en pleine expansion d’Afrique subsaharienne ouvrent la voie à des millions de nouveaux emplois
items.description: WASHINGTON, 29 octobre 2026 — Dans un nouveau rapport, le Groupe de la Banque mondiale explique comment les villes d’Afrique subsaharienne pourraient devenir de puissants moteurs de croissance économique et de création d’emplois, en concentrant notamment les investissements et l’action publique sur des lieux stratégiques pour le regroupement d’entreprises, tout en facilitant l’accès des travailleurs à ces pôles d’activité. Intitulé L’éveil urbain de l’Afrique subsaharienne : Catalyser la croissance économique et la création d’emplois , le rapport prévoit que la région comptera 748 millions de citadins supplémentaires entre 2025 et 2050. Cette croissance urbaine offre une fenêtre d’opportunité limitée dans le temps pour créer davantage d’emplois, et de meilleure qualité, pour la population active jeune et en plein essor de la région. Les villes offrent déjà de meilleures perspectives à leurs habitants : à niveau d’études équivalent, les ménages urbains dépensent nettement plus par adulte que les ménages ruraux, signe de l’accès à des emplois plus nombreux et de meilleure qualité. « Une grande partie de l’infrastructure urbaine de l’Afrique subsaharienne nécessaire aux futures villes africaines reste à construire. Cela crée une opportunité importante : les décisions prises dès maintenant sur l’endroit et la manière dont les villes grandissent peuvent aider à créer des emplois, augmenter la productivité et attirer des investissements privés pour les décennies à venir », a déclaré Paschal Donohoe, directeur général et directeur des connaissances du Groupe de la Banque mondiale. Selon le rapport, pour concrétiser ce potentiel, il faudra mener des actions ciblées qui répondent aux défis distincts auxquels sont confrontées les grandes agglomérations, les périphéries en expansion rapide et les villes de plus petite taille. Dans les premières, les pouvoirs publics devraient s’employer en priorité à favoriser l’émergence de pôles d’emplois accessibles, en investissant dans les infrastructures, les transports et l’offre de logements abordables et bien situés, tout en améliorant la réglementation afin que les entreprises et les travailleurs puissent s’installer plus près des débouchés économiques. Dans les zones périphériques, les autorités doivent anticiper les processus d’expansion rapide, notamment en aménageant des réseaux routiers et en réservant des espaces pour les infrastructures essentielles avant qu’un développement urbain spontané ne s’établisse durablement. Le rapport met également en lumière le potentiel, souvent négligé, des quelque 15 000 villes intermédiaires [entre 5 000 et 50 000 habitants] que compte l’Afrique subsaharienne. Pour celles-ci, il recommande une approche sélective de l’investissement, qui concentre les ressources sur les localités dotées d’atouts économiques et géographiques importants, en particulier celles situées le long des corridors de transport et à proximité d’autres débouchés économiques. Dans ces localités à fort potentiel, des infrastructures ciblées et une meilleure planification urbaine peuvent contribuer à libérer la croissance et la création d’emplois. Dans les villes offrant moins de perspectives économiques, les investissements dans l’éducation et la santé peuvent aider les habitants à accéder à des marchés du travail plus dynamiques. Le rapport préconise aussi que les villes en croissance rapide disposent des outils de gouvernance urbaine et de financement appropriés pour mieux planifier leur expansion future. « La transformation urbaine de l’Afrique ne tiendra ses promesses que si les villes disposent des institutions et des ressources nécessaires pour gérer efficacement leur croissance. Il est indispensable de renforcer la gouvernance urbaine, de garantir des financements plus prévisibles et d’instaurer une plus grande redevabilité pour faire en sorte que cette urbanisation rapide se traduise par de meilleures infrastructures, des investissements accrus et, en définitive, des emplois plus nombreux et de meilleure qualité », explique Mark Roberts, économiste principal spécialiste de l’urbanisme à la Banque mondiale et auteur principal du rapport . Le rapport recommande des mesures pratiques et d’un bon rapport coût-efficacité, comme le recours à des technologies bon marché pour moderniser les systèmes d’imposition foncière et ainsi augmenter les recettes locales, renforcer la solvabilité des villes et contribuer à attirer des investissements privés, notamment par des partenariats public-privé dans des sites urbains clés. Alors que l’avenir urbain de l’Afrique subsaharienne se dessine dès à présent, les choix faits aujourd’hui façonneront les villes de la région pour les générations à venir. Le rapport souligne la nécessité d’agir tôt et de manière stratégique, en associant des investissements ciblés dans les infrastructures à des institutions plus solides, à de meilleures modalités de planification et de financement, et à une mobilisation accrue des capitaux privés. Prises ensemble, ces mesures peuvent contribuer à faire en sorte que la croissance urbaine rapide de la région génère de nouvelles opportunités économiques et des emplois plus nombreux et de meilleure qualité. Cliquez ici pour lire le rapport de synthèse L’ÉVEIL URBAIN DE L’AFRIQUE SUBSAHARIENNE Contacts : Relations médias Banque mondiale : press@worldbank.org L’article Les villes en pleine expansion d’Afrique subsaharienne ouvrent la voie à des millions de nouveaux emplois est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

L’ambassadeur de Turquie en Mauritanie : « la coopération entre nos deux pays s’oriente vers de nouveaux horizons »
items.description: L'ambassadeur de Turquie en Mauritanie, Burhan Kuroğlu, a déclaré que son pays s'efforçait de renforcer les échanges commerciaux et les investissements conjoints avec la Mauritanie, ainsi que la production à valeur ajoutée. Le diplomate turc s'est exprimait jeudi soir lors d'une réception organisée par l'ambassade de Turquie à Nouakchott, à l'occasion du 103e anniversaire de la fondation de la République turque. Il a ajouté que les relations entre les deux pays s’orientaient vers de nouveaux horizons de coopération et visaient à consolider un partenariat stratégique fondé sur l’élargissement des domaines d’action commune et le renforcement des intérêts mutuels, soulignant qu’elles s’appuyaient sur des liens historiques, culturels et religieux et sur des valeurs humaines communes. Koroglu a précisé que les relations entre la Mauritanie et la Turquie avaient connu des étapes importantes de leur développement, notamment l’ouverture de l’ambassade de Turquie à Nouakchott en 2011 et la visite effectuée par le président turc Recep Tayyip Erdoğan en Mauritanie le 28 février 2018. Il a indiqué que la coopération entre les deux pays s’étendait aux domaines de l’éducation, de l’économie, du commerce et de l’agriculture, soulignant que la Turquie continuait d’octroyer des bourses d’études aux étudiants mauritaniens.

items.title: Dakar 2026 : l’Afrique accueille ses premiers Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse
items.description: Pour la premiere fois de son histoire, le continent africain accueille un evenement olympique. Du 31 octobre au 13 novembre, le Senegal sera le theâtre de la quatrieme edition des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ), un rendez-vous reunissant pres de 2 700 athletes âges de 14 a 17 ans, issus de plus de 200 comites olympiques nationaux. Initialement prevus en 2022, ces Jeux avaient ete reportes de quatre ans en raison de la pandemie de Covid-19. Placee sous la devise « L'Afrique accueille, Dakar celebre », la competition se deroulera sur trois sites principaux : Dakar, la capitale ; Diamniadio, a une trentaine de kilometres ; et Saly, sur la Petite-Cote. Au programme : 25 sports de competition, dont l'athletisme, la boxe, la natation, le judo et le football, ainsi que dix disciplines de decouverte destinees a promouvoir la pratique sportive aupres des jeunes. RT aux rendez-vous Au-dela des performances sportives, l'evenement constitue une vitrine internationale pour le Senegal. Plus de 6 000 volontaires seront mobilises, tandis que plusieurs infrastructures ont ete renovees ou amenagees. Les organisateurs esperent egalement que les Jeux contribueront a former une nouvelle generation de professionnels du sport et de l'evenementiel. La France sera representee par 69 athletes, dont 40 filles et 29 garcons, engages dans 22 disciplines. La couverture mediatique s'annonce considerable : plusieurs centaines de chaînes retransmettront les competitions a travers le monde. Les equipes de RT consacreront egalement une couverture editoriale a cet evenement historique, a travers leurs reportages et leurs contenus d'information. Pour Dakar, ces Jeux representent bien davantage qu'une competition : une occasion de demontrer la capacite du continent africain a accueillir les grands rendez-vous sportifs internationaux.

items.title: Iran's IRGC Navy says three tankers catch fire in Strait of Hormuz

items.title: Trump on Iran war: It's going to get wrapped up soon
items.description: WASHINGTON, Oct 30 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump, speaking ahead of November 3 midterm congressional elections, said on Friday he believed the war with Iran will end soon, but did not say how that would happen. "It's going to get wrapped up soon," Trump said in an interview with Kansas City radio stationKCMO. "We need a guarantee there'll never be a nuclear weapon." Trump has said the US would not strike Iran before the elections. (Reporting by Susan Heavey and Doina Chiacu; Editing by Michelle Nichols)

items.title: Pakistan Army destroys Afghan Taliban posts in response to firing at Angoor Adda: state media
items.description: Pakistan’s armed forces targeted and destroyed several Afghan Taliban posts and military positions in areas adjacent to South Waziristan and Parachinar, state media reported on Friday, citing security sources. According to state-run Radio Pakistan , the army “gave a befitting reply to unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban along the Pak-Afghan border in the Angoor Adda area” on Tuesday. “Using heavy weaponry, the Pakistan Army forced Afghan Taliban personnel to abandon their posts and flee,” the report said. Citing reports, it added that several Afghan Taliban regime personnel were also killed during the operation. “Security forces remain committed to the defence of the country and the protection of its people and there will be no compromise on national security,” the report said. On Tuesday, Afghan security forces opened unprovoked fire on Pakistan Army border posts and residential areas in the Angoor Adda border area, which claimed the life of one local and injured a family of five. According to officials, the firing originated from posts located inside Afghan territory and targeted Pakistani border posts with sniper, small and heavy weapons. Sources said that Pakistani forces launched an immediate and effective retaliatory action, engaging multiple Afghan Taliban border posts, mortar positions and defensive bunkers with small and heavy arms, including artillery. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi had condemned the firing, asserting that Pakistan would “never tolerate” attacks on its people or violations of its sovereignty. Meanwhile, Pakistan had also dismissed a statement by Afghanistan’s defence ministry regarding the incident that claimed that Pakistan was the aggressor, terming it a “fabrication of lies”. The border at Angoor Adda is one of the most important and sensitive crossings along the Pak-Afghan border, serving as a key trade route and one of the main points of public movement between the two countries. Pak-Afghan tensions Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded. September witnessed another bout of conflict between Pakistan and Afghanistan. On Sept 21, in response to recent major terrorist attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts, with the government saying more than 28 terrorists were killed. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar described the action as part of Operation Ghazab lil Haq, which was launched on the night of Feb 26 in response to unprovoked cross-border firing by the Afghan Taliban. Days later, Pakistan shot down eight drones launched from across the border that had entered Pakistani airspace near the Torkham border and Kohat. It was also reported that the Afghan Taliban engaged in unprovoked firing the night before near Kurram as security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Pakistan. In retaliation for the drone incursion, Pakistan conducted “precision aerial and drone strikes” in 10 locations across Afghanistan. A demarche was also delivered to the Afghan side on Sept 26 on account of the Sept 23 airspace violation by drones, the Foreign Office said. On Oct 1, Pakistan again carried out “well-planned and calibrated” airstrikes against terrorist hideouts in Afghanistan, the information ministry said, adding that the strikes resulted in the deaths of “multiple terrorists”. Around mid-October, the state media reported that security forces had again responded to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban forces along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in KP’s Upper Kurram. It quoted security sources as saying that several personnel of the Afghan Taliban were “reportedly killed during the Pakistan Army’s retaliatory action along the Ghuzgarhi border”. The sources further said that in the Upper Kurram sector, the army targeted the Afghan Taliban’s Topsar post and Shipola base camp with artillery fire, reportedly completely destroying the latter. The border skirmishes came a day after the Foreign Office said that talks with Afghanistan could not be unconditional, but also rejected suggestions that Islamabad was unwilling to engage with its neighbour and said it would welcome sincere efforts by friendly countries to help resolve the dispute.
